title: Constructibility of localizing exceptional cohomology
statement: Fix a universe $u$, a prime $\ell$, and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. Let $Z,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes in universe $u$, and $g:Z\to Y$ a proper $k$-morphism [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring with its specified multiplication and a certificate of one of the three adic coefficient families [def-sfb-adic-coefficient-certificate]; the algebraic-closure coefficient has the finite-subextension-valued meaning of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. For $T=Z,Y$, put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$, $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and let $\mathcal B_T$ be its bounded constructible full subcategory [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], using constructibility in the stratified local-finite-presentation sense [def-sfb-constructible-module]. Let $\mathcal L_T=\operatorname{Loc}(\mathcal B_T)$ be the full localizing hull formed with ambient coproducts indexed in universe $u+1$ [def-sfb-bounded-constructible-localizing-closure], and $F_g:\mathcal L_Z\to\mathcal L_Y$ the canonical restriction of the actual ambient $Rg_*$ [lem-sfb-adic-proper-localizing-pushforward]. For every functor $G:\mathcal L_Y\to\mathcal L_Z$, every supplied adjunction $F_g\dashv G$, every $K\in\mathcal B_Y$, and every integer $n$, the module $H^n(G(K))$ in $\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_Z}$ is constructible in the sense of [def-sfb-constructible-module]. Here $K$ enters $\mathcal L_Y$ by the canonical full inclusion, and cohomology is taken after the full inclusion $\mathcal L_Z\hookrightarrow D_Z$. No derived-completeness condition is imposed.

lean.statement: theorem ellAdic_localizing_rightAdjoint_obj_homology_constructible (G : (boundedConstructibleLocalizingClosure Λ Y.left).FullSubcategory ⥤ (boundedConstructibleLocalizingClosure Λ Z.left).FullSubcategory) (adj : ellAdicLocalizingLowerStar Λ ℓ g hΛ ⊣ G) (K : (boundedConstructible (condensedRingObj Λ Y.left)).FullSubcategory) : ∀ n : ℤ, IsConstructibleModuleObject (condensedRingObj Λ Z.left) ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ n).obj ((G.obj ((boundedConstructibleToLocalizing Λ Y.left).obj K)).obj))

proof.text: The finite-type structure maps over the field give locally Noetherian schemes and compact underlying spaces by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Separatedness gives quasi-separatedness. Their Noetherian scheme structures give Noetherian underlying spaces by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]; every locally closed stratum inherits this through its embedding. These are precisely the hypotheses of the coefficient comparisons below.

source.place: Coefficient comparison and proper adjoint restriction, Lean proof step 1

proof.text: Normalize each certificate of [def-sfb-adic-coefficient-certificate] to the coefficient conventions of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. For a finite normed extension E, choose the Mathlib algebra embedding IsAlgClosed.lift into the fixed PadicAlgCl, and use AlgHom.equivFieldRange to identify E with its finite-dimensional intermediate-field image. The algebra equivalence and inverse are continuous by finite-dimensional linear-map continuity. Postcomposition gives inverse morphisms of continuous-map ring sheaves, hence a monoid-object isomorphism. For integral E use the already specified embedding into PadicAlgCl. Its field-range equivalence carries the norm-at-most-one subring onto the corresponding integral subring by definition; its restriction is an isometry, and again postcomposition gives the condensed ring isomorphism. The finite-subextension-valued algebraic closure case is the identity. The Lean helpers continuousCoefficientIso, continuousCoefficient_normalize and integralCoefficient_normalize perform these constructions explicitly; no unproved existence theorem is used to define data.

source.place: Coefficient comparison and proper adjoint restriction, Lean proof step 2

proof.text: Compare the two module-constructibility predicates over the normalized coefficients. For the field and finite-subextension-valued algebraic-closure cases, use the finite-free cover consequences of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-lfp-local-triviality] and [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qbar-lfp-local-triviality] on each Noetherian stratum. A finite free module is the pullback of the finite free module over the point, with its zero-map cokernel presentation, and is therefore a finite constant local model. The converse is local finite presentation of finite constant models [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. For the integral case use [lem-sfb-integral-lfp-constant-model-comparison], including its existing ULift/spectral-norm coefficient isomorphism. Coefficient isomorphisms preserve the explicit cokernel presentations by scalar comap; applying comap by the inverse proves the converse. The pullback/comap and isomorphism transport are the APIs of [lem-weil-pbc-module-constructible-pullback]. Thus IsConstantModelConstructible is equivalent to IsConstructibleModuleObject for each cohomology module. The boundedness condition is literally identical, so the bounded constructible object properties coincide.

source.place: Coefficient comparison and proper adjoint restriction, Lean proof step 3

proof.text: Apply [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc] to identify constant-model Dctf and Dbc. The bounded-constructible hull [def-sfb-bounded-constructible-localizing-closure] equals localizingClosureOfSize with indexing universe u+1: prove both inclusions from the defining universal properties, installing the replete triangulated and coproduct-closed structures of the intersection. The universe comparison closure_index_eq from the proof API of [det-proper-image-localizing-principle] identifies the ordinary ambient localizing closure with this same sized closure, in the module-object derived category whose Hom universe is u+1. Combining these equalities with the previous step identifies both hulls as object properties in the same ordinary derived category.

source.place: Coefficient comparison and proper adjoint restriction, Lean proof step 4

proof.text: The normalized coefficients satisfy IsLocalizingAdmissibleCoefficient. Apply [sk-thm-existence] to obtain an adjunction for the specified compactification lower shriek, together with preservation of Dctf by its right adjoint J. This uses the already-stated preservation clause rather than repeating its rational/integral case proof. For the proper morphism apply [det-cor-existence-ii-restriction] to identify this lower shriek with the restriction of the actual ambient derived pushforward. Transport its adjunction along that natural isomorphism. Its left functor is the same ambient pushforward restriction as [lem-sfb-adic-proper-localizing-pushforward], after the hull equalities of the previous step.

source.place: Coefficient comparison and proper adjoint restriction, Lean proof step 5

proof.text: The private generic helper rightAdjoint_preserves_of_eq eliminates the two equalities of object properties; membership witnesses for the resulting identical lifts agree by proof irrelevance. Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] to J and the supplied G, and apply the fully faithful ambient inclusion to its component on K. Dctf=Dbc and the comparison in step 3 say J(K) is bounded constructible for the original predicate. Boundedness is isomorphism invariant, and applying each homology functor to the ambient isomorphism transports constructibility via [lem-weil-pbc-module-constructible-pullback]. Hence G(K) is bounded constructible. Project its constructible-cohomology component to obtain exactly the claimed conclusion for every integer n.
